```{r setup}
library(tidyverse); library(knitr)
S <- readRDS("output/overall_v1_stats.rds")
fp  <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
fpc <- function(x) sprintf("%+.0f%%", x)
ci  <- function(lo, hi) sprintf("%+.0f to %+.0f%%", lo, hi)
tab <- function(d, cap, ...) kable(d, booktabs = TRUE, caption = cap, linesep = "", ...)
slope_tab <- function(d, cap) tab(d %>% transmute(Light = color, `% per km` = fpc(pct_per_km), `95% CI` = ci(lo, hi),
                                                  z = sprintf("%.2f", z), p = fp(p)), cap, align = "lrrrr")
model_tab <- function(d) tab(d %>% transmute(Model = model, `Obs.` = n_obs, Stations = n_sites, Family = family,
                                             `Converged` = ifelse(converged, "yes", "no")),
                             "Models (negative binomial GLMMs; site random intercept).", align = "lrrll")
```

All percentages are back-transformed from the log scale: % change in detections per km away from the parking lot, or % difference under white vs. red light. 95% CIs are Wald intervals; p-values are Wald z-tests. "Holm" and "BH" mark p-values adjusted across the five intensities (Holm) or across the taxa tested (Benjamini–Hochberg). Light color and intensity were set experimentally; distance is observational.

```{r report-helpers}
jt  <- function(set, tax, term) { r <- S[[set]]$joint %>% filter(taxon == tax, term == !!term)
  sprintf("$\\chi^2_{%d}$ = %.2f, p %s", r$df, r$chisq, ifelse(r$p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", sprintf("%.3f", r$p)))) }
pp  <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p))
sl  <- function(d, col = NULL) { r <- if (is.null(col)) d else d[d$color == col, ]
  sprintf("%+.0f%% per km, 95%% CI %+.0f to %+.0f%%, %s", r$pct_per_km, r$lo, r$hi, pp(r$p)) }
F2  <- S$fig2
rng <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f–%.0f%%", min(abs(x)), max(abs(x)))
bw  <- F2$bat_wvr %>% filter(intensity %in% c("30%", "50%", "70%"))
mw  <- F2$moth_wvr %>% filter(intensity != "100%")
md  <- F2$moth_dist %>% filter(p_holm < 0.05)
f4s <- S$fig4 %>% filter(significant) %>% arrange(p_BH)
```

## Reading and reporting the results

Each figure answers a question at two levels, and they should be reported in that order:

1. **The interaction test**: does the effect differ between conditions (light colors, intensities)? This is one joint Wald $\chi^2$ test per model term, from the same model as the figure.
2. **The effects the figure plots**: the distance slope or white-vs-red difference within each condition, as % change with 95% CI and its (adjusted) p-value.

The asterisks in the figures belong to level 2: each tests whether *that* condition's effect differs from zero. They do not test whether conditions differ from each other. A starred and an unstarred condition are only "different" when the interaction test says so; when it does not, describe the effect as shared across conditions.

```{r joint-table, results = "asis"}
jtab <- bind_rows(mutate(S$fig1$joint, set = "11 stations (Figures 1–2)"),
                  mutate(S$fig5$joint, set = "13 stations (Figure 5)")) %>%
  mutate(question = recode(term,
           dist_km = "Distance slope, averaged over color and intensity",
           `color:dist_km` = "Does the distance slope differ between red and white?",
           `intensity:dist_km` = "Does the distance slope differ among intensities?",
           `color:intensity` = "Does the white vs. red difference depend on intensity?"),
         fig = recode(term, dist_km = "1B–C / 5B–C", `color:dist_km` = "1B–C / 5B–C",
                      `intensity:dist_km` = "2A–B", `color:intensity` = "2C–D"),
         term = factor(term, c("dist_km", "color:dist_km", "intensity:dist_km", "color:intensity"))) %>%
  arrange(set, term, taxon)
blank <- function(x) ifelse(x == lag(x, default = ""), "", x)
for (st in unique(jtab$set))
  print(tab(jtab %>% filter(set == st) %>%
              transmute(Figure = blank(fig), Question = blank(question), Taxon = taxon,
                        `Chi-sq (df)` = sprintf("%.2f (%d)", chisq, df), p = fp(p)),
            paste0("Interaction tests, ", st, ": joint Wald chi-square tests (emmeans::joint\\_tests) from the models behind the figures."),
            align = "lllrr"))
```

### Methods paragraph (template)

> Bat detections per site-night and moth specimens per trap night were modeled with negative binomial GLMMs (glmmTMB, nbinom2) including light color × intensity, intensity × distance, color × distance, moon phase, non-forest cover, sky brightness (lights off), day of year (linear and quadratic) and a random intercept for station. Light color and intensity were assigned by night; distance from the lit parking lot is observational. We tested each interaction with a joint Wald $\chi^2$ test and then estimated distance slopes and white-vs-red contrasts within each condition (emmeans), back-transformed to % change per km or % difference. P-values across the five intensities were Holm-adjusted. For the taxonomic hierarchies, zero-inflated negative binomial GLMMs with a taxon × distance interaction were fitted at each level, and p-values were adjusted across taxa with the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure.

### Example results, figure by figure

**Figure 1B — bats (color × distance not significant, so report one shared slope).** Bat detections declined with distance from the lot (`r sl(S$fig1$common %>% filter(taxon == "Bats"))`), and the decline did not differ between red and white light (color × distance `r jt("fig1", "Bats", "color:dist_km")`). *Avoid:* reporting the red and white slopes as two separate findings.

**Figure 1C — moths (color × distance significant, so report each color).** The moth distance gradient depended on light color (`r jt("fig1", "Moths", "color:dist_km")`): under white light, catches rose away from the lot (`r sl(S$fig1$moth_slopes, "White")`), whereas under red light there was no gradient (`r sl(S$fig1$moth_slopes, "Red")`).

**Figure 2A — bats (intensity × distance not significant, so describe consistency).** The bat decline with distance did not differ significantly among intensities (`r jt("fig1", "Bats", "intensity:dist_km")`); slopes ranged from `r sprintf("%+.0f", max(F2$bat_dist$pct_per_km))` to `r sprintf("%+.0f", min(F2$bat_dist$pct_per_km))`% per km at every intensity. *Avoid:* "bats declined only at 100%"; the 100% slope is the one individually clear of zero after Holm adjustment, not one that differs from the others.

**Figure 2B — moths (intensity × distance significant, so per-intensity results can be interpreted).** The moth gradient depended on intensity (`r jt("fig1", "Moths", "intensity:dist_km")`): catches rose away from the lot at `r paste(sprintf("%s (%+.0f%% per km, Holm %s)", md$intensity, md$pct_per_km, pp(md$p_holm)), collapse = " and ")`, with no clear gradient at the other intensities.

**Figure 2C–D (color × intensity significant for both, so report each intensity's contrast).** The white vs. red difference depended on intensity for bats (`r jt("fig1", "Bats", "color:intensity")`) and moths (`r jt("fig1", "Moths", "color:intensity")`). Bats were `r rng(bw$pct_white_vs_red)` less active under white than red light at 30–70% intensity (all Holm p at most `r sprintf("%.3f", max(bw$p_holm))`), with no difference at 10%. Moths showed no color difference at 10–70% (all Holm p at least `r sprintf("%.2f", min(mw$p_holm))`). At 100%, the differences reverse for bats (`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", F2$bat_wvr$pct_white_vs_red[5])`) and are large for moths (`r sprintf("%+.0f%%", F2$moth_wvr$pct_white_vs_red[5])`); report these with the caveat that the red-light 100% nights include the July full moon and the two wettest nights of the study.

**Figures 3–4 (hierarchies): report the count tested, the count significant, and each node's slope with its adjusted p.** Of `r nrow(S$fig4)` moth taxa tested, `r nrow(f4s)` changed significantly with distance after Benjamini–Hochberg correction, all increasing away from the lot (e.g. `r f4s$taxon[1]`, `r sprintf("%+.0f%% per km", f4s$pct_per_km[1])`, adjusted `r pp(f4s$p_BH[1])`). For bats, give the all-bats slope (single test) and the guild and species slopes BH-adjusted across the 12 nodes (Figure 3 table).

**Figure 5 (sensitivity analysis with the far stations).** Including the two far stations (0–7.5 km), the bat gradient disappeared (`r sl(S$fig5$common %>% filter(taxon == "Bats"))`), while moths still increased away from the lot under white light (`r sl(S$fig5$moth_slopes, "White")`) but not under red (`r sl(S$fig5$moth_slopes, "Red")`; color × distance `r jt("fig5", "Moths", "color:dist_km")`).

### General rules

- Lead with the effect size and its 95% CI; the p-value comes second.
- Never infer that two conditions differ because one is significant and the other is not; cite the interaction test.
- State the adjustment for every family of tests: Holm across the five intensities, BH across hierarchy nodes or taxa, none for single tests.
- Distance is observational ("associated with distance from the lot"); light color and intensity were randomized by night, so causal wording is appropriate for them.

## Model formulas

All models are fitted with `glmmTMB` (negative binomial, `nbinom2`). `site` is a random intercept; light `color` (R/W) and `intensity` (10, 30, 50, 70, 100%) are factors; `dist_km` = distance from the parking lot; `jd_c` = day of year, centered.

**Figures 1B–C, 2 and 5B–C** — one model per taxon (Figures 1–2: 11 stations; Figure 5: 13 stations, GRTE15 excluded). Figure 1 uses the color × distance slopes; Figure 2 uses the intensity × distance slopes (A–B) and the color × intensity contrasts (C–D).

```{r formulas, results = "asis"}
fmt <- function(f) {   # treatment terms first, then covariates, then random effects; wrapped at ~85 characters
  parts <- strsplit(f, " ~ ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  terms <- trimws(strsplit(parts[2], " + ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])
  ord <- c(grep(":", terms, value = TRUE), intersect(c("color", "intensity", "dist_km"), terms),
           setdiff(terms[!grepl(":|\\|", terms)], c("color", "intensity", "dist_km")), grep("\\|", terms, value = TRUE))
  lines <- character(0); cur <- paste(parts[1], "~")
  for (t in ord) {
    add <- if (grepl("~$", cur)) paste(cur, t) else paste(cur, "+", t)
    if (nchar(add) > 85) { lines <- c(lines, cur); cur <- paste("  +", t) } else cur <- add
  }
  paste(c(lines, cur), collapse = "\n")
}
cat("Bats (total detections per site-night; no zero-inflation):\n\n```\n", fmt(S$fig1$models$formula[1]), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
cat("Moths (specimens per trap night; no zero-inflation):\n\n```\n", fmt(S$fig1$models$formula[2]), "\n```\n\n", sep = "")
```

**Figure 3 — bat hierarchy** (zero-inflated, `ziformula = ~1`; zero-filled site-nights). All bats uses total detections; guilds and species use their own detections with `taxon` = guild or species. Every tier converged with the full covariate set.

```
All bats:          total_det ~ dist_km + color + intensity + mean_phase + pct_nonforest
                     + brightness_dark + jd_c + I(jd_c^2) + (1 | site)
Guilds / species:  detections ~ taxon * dist_km + color + intensity + mean_phase
                     + pct_nonforest + brightness_dark + jd_c + I(jd_c^2) + (1 | site)
```

**Figure 4 — moth hierarchy** (zero-inflated, `ziformula = ~1`; one model per taxonomic level over the taxa with at least 30 site-nights, zero-filled trap nights). If a level's model did not converge, covariates were dropped in this order: non-forest cover, sky brightness, season², moon phase.

```
detections ~ taxon * dist_km + color + intensity + mean_phase + pct_nonforest
  + brightness_dark + jd_c + I(jd_c^2) + (1 | site)
```

In both hierarchies a node's slope and p-value come from the taxon-specific `dist_km` slope (`emtrends`); curves are averaged over color and intensity.

## Figure 1A and 5A: Station sky brightness

```{r sky}
tab(S$sky %>% transmute(Station = paste0(site, ifelse(lot, " (lot)", "")), `Distance (km)` = sprintf("%.2f", dist_km),
                        `Lights off (DSU)` = sprintf("%.1f", lights_off),
                        `White 100% (DSU)` = ifelse(white100_filled, "—", sprintf("%.1f", white100)),
                        `Mapped (DSU)` = paste0(sprintf("%.1f", white100_map), ifelse(white100_filled, "*", "")),
                        `In Figure 1` = ifelse(far, "no (far)", "yes")),
    "Sky brightness from the fisheye photos (dark sky units). Lights off = darkest lights-off photo (as used in the models); white 100% = mean of three photos (GRTE11 p1 excluded: transient light). Distance from the reference point at GRTE17.",
    align = "lrrrrl")
```

\* No white-light photos; the lights-off value is mapped instead. GRTE15 appears in neither map. The surface in the maps is inverse-distance-weighted interpolation of log DSU (power 2), clipped to 300 m around the stations.

## Figure 1B–C: Distance slopes by light color (11 stations, 0–2.1 km)

```{r f1}
model_tab(S$fig1$models)
```

Both models: color × intensity, intensity × distance, color × distance, moon phase, non-forest cover, sky brightness (lights off), season (day of year, linear + quadratic) and a site random intercept. Full formulas: see *Model formulas* above.

```{r f1s}
slope_tab(S$fig1$bat_slopes, "Figure 1B — bats: % change in detections per km under each light color (not adjusted).")
slope_tab(S$fig1$moth_slopes, "Figure 1C — moths: % change in specimens per km under each light color (not adjusted).")
```

## Figure 2: Effects at each light intensity (same models as Figure 1)

```{r f2}
int_tab <- function(d, est, cap) tab(d %>% transmute(Intensity = intensity, Estimate = fpc(.data[[est]]), `95% CI` = ci(lo, hi),
                                                     z = sprintf("%.2f", z), p = fp(p), `p (Holm)` = fp(p_holm)), cap, align = "lrrrrr")
int_tab(S$fig2$bat_dist,  "pct_per_km",       "Figure 2A — bats: % change in detections per km away from the lot, by intensity.")
int_tab(S$fig2$moth_dist, "pct_per_km",       "Figure 2B — moths: % change in specimens per km away from the lot, by intensity.")
int_tab(S$fig2$bat_wvr,   "pct_white_vs_red", "Figure 2C — bats: % difference under white vs. red light, by intensity (at the mean distance).")
int_tab(S$fig2$moth_wvr,  "pct_white_vs_red", "Figure 2D — moths: % difference under white vs. red light, by intensity (at the mean distance).")
```

Red-light nights at 100% intensity: moth traps 4 nights (12–13 July, 5–6 August 2022), bat detectors 6 nights (11–13 July, 4–6 August); they include the July full moon and the two wettest nights of the study.

## Figure 3: Bat distance hierarchy (11 stations)

```{r f3}
tab(S$fig3 %>% transmute(Tier = tier, Taxon = taxon, `% per km` = fpc(pct_per_km), `95% CI` = ci(lo, hi),
                         z = sprintf("%.2f", z), `p (raw)` = fp(p_raw), `p (adj.)` = fp(p_adj)),
    "Figure 3 — distance slope at each node. All bats: single test (unadjusted); guilds and species: Benjamini–Hochberg across the 12 nodes.",
    align = "llrrrrr")
```

Zero-inflated negative binomial GLMMs of detections per site-night (all bats = total; guild and species = their detections, zero-filled) with taxon × distance, light color, intensity, moon phase, non-forest cover, sky brightness, season and a site random intercept. Covariates were dropped in order if a model did not converge; covariates used: all bats — `r unique(S$fig3$covariates[S$fig3$tier == "All bats"])`; guilds — `r unique(S$fig3$covariates[S$fig3$tier == "Guild"])`; species — `r unique(S$fig3$covariates[S$fig3$tier == "Species"])`.

## Figure 4: Moth distance hierarchy (11 stations)

```{r f4}
sig <- S$fig4 %>% filter(significant)
tab(sig %>% transmute(Level = level, Taxon = taxon, `% per km` = fpc(pct_per_km), `p (raw)` = fp(p_raw), `p (BH)` = fp(p_BH)),
    sprintf("Figure 4 — the %d taxa shown: Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted p < 0.05 across all %d taxa tested.", nrow(sig), nrow(S$fig4)),
    align = "llrrr")
```

Taxon × distance zero-inflated negative binomial GLMM at each taxonomic level (taxa with at least 30 site-nights), with light color, intensity, moon phase, non-forest cover, sky brightness, season and a site random intercept.

```{r f4all}
tab(S$fig4 %>% filter(!significant) %>% transmute(Level = level, Taxon = taxon, `% per km` = fpc(pct_per_km),
                                                   `p (raw)` = fp(p_raw), `p (BH)` = fp(p_BH)),
    "All other taxa tested (not significant after adjustment).", align = "llrrr", longtable = TRUE)
```

## Figure 5B–C: Distance slopes with the far stations (13 stations, 0–7.5 km; GRTE15 excluded)

```{r f5}
model_tab(S$fig5$models)
slope_tab(S$fig5$bat_slopes, "Figure 5B — bats: % change in detections per km under each light color (not adjusted).")
slope_tab(S$fig5$moth_slopes, "Figure 5C — moths: % change in specimens per km under each light color (not adjusted).")
```

Same model structure as Figure 1B–C, fitted on the 13 stations.
